tweets.text:
Emerging market bond spreads sit near 200 basis points, close to the lowest in a generation.

In the 1998 Asian crisis, investors demanded over 1,500 basis points of extra yield to hold EM sovereign debt ($EMB). Today they take about 200, even as developed-market bonds sell off and 30-year yields hit new highs.

Either emerging markets have truly de-risked, or the reach for yield has crushed the premium for real risk. At 200 basis points, there is almost no cushion left if that bet is wrong.

Binance is the largest crypto exchange on Earth. In Europe it now ranks 6th.

In July and August, Revolut X led European crypto app downloads with 438,000. Binance managed 114,000, behind Revolut, OKX, Kraken, Bybit, and Coinbase. In euro-denominated spot volume, Binance holds roughly 3%.

The reason is a license. Binance failed to secure EU MiCA approval, and regulated rivals took the continent. In markets with real rules, compliance is the moat, and the incumbent that skipped it is losing.

Traders now use crypto exchanges to bet on stocks and commodities.

These real-world-asset perps went from near zero to more than 20% of crypto-venue volume in under a year. In August, $778 billion of them ran through the platforms. The plumbing built for Bitcoin is now a shadow market for the S&P 500 and oil.

This leverage runs 24/7, offshore, with no closing bell and no circuit breakers. When the next selloff hits, it unwinds first where nobody regulates it, a fresh channel for contagion.

The US 30-year sits near 5%, the UK near 5.5%, and Japan, pinned near zero for a generation, now pays 3.5%. Governments are flooding the market with debt, and buyers demand more yield to hold it.
